general_lore: Vvardenfell is a volcanic island in Morrowind ruled by the Dunmer Tribunal Temple and three Great Houses: House Hlaalu (cunning merchants friendly to the Empire), House Redoran (pious, honorable warriors living in Skar), and House Telvanni (eccentric, power-mad wizards living in giant mushroom towers). The native Dunmer are highly suspicious of foreign 'Outlanders', who arrive via boat to Seyda Neen. The Temple worships the living gods Vivec, Almalexia, and Sotha Sil, but their authority is challenged by Ashlander nomads, outlander Imperial guilds, and the dark ash-storms blowing from the volcano where the devil Dagoth Ur dwells.
faction_notes: Temple priests are devoted, charity-focused, and suspicious of foreign gods. Imperial Legionnaires are formal, law-abiding, and complain about Vvardenfell's heat. Mages Guild scholars are academic, snobbish, and compete with the wild Telvanni wizards. The native Camonna Tong syndicate hates foreign outlanders and works to destroy the imported Thieves Guild. The Morag Tong is a legally sanctioned guild of honorable assassins.
geographic_notes: Seyda Neen is a swampy, mud-slick Imperial tax post. Balmora is the Hlaalu trading hub situated along the Odai River. Vivec is a massive metropolis built on water cantons. Ald'ruhn is a dusty Redoran stronghold constantly battered by ashstorms. Sadrith Mora is the Telvanni wizard sanctuary grown from giant mushrooms.
landmass_lore_note: Used when the player is NOT on Vvardenfell (general_lore above is Vvardenfell's). Edit any entry to change what NPCs believe about that land; leave one empty to use the built-in text.

landmass_lore.solstheim: Solstheim is a frozen island of pine forest, snowfields and glaciers. The Nordic Skaal live in their village in harmony with the All-Maker, the Imperial Legion holds Fort Frostmoth, and the East Empire Company runs the ebony mining colony of Raven Rock. Thirsk mead hall stands on a lake in the north.
landmass_lore.morrowind_mainland: The Morrowind mainland is the old Dunmer heartland across the Inner Sea from Vvardenfell. Great House Indoril holds the orthodox Temple lands around Mournhold, Great House Dres keeps its slave plantations in the southern swamps, Telvanni wizards rule mushroom towers along the north-eastern coasts and isles, and Hlaalu traders push into the west. Old Ebonheart is the Imperial seat of the province, and Necrom is the holy city of the dead. Vvardenfell, Red Mountain and the Blight are across the water; mainlanders know of them mostly as news, pilgrim stories and worried rumours.
landmass_lore.skyrim: Skyrim is the cold homeland of the Nords: highlands, heaths, pine forests, snowfields and rivers. Nordic jarls rule the holds under the High King and the Empire, and the Imperial Legion patrols the roads. In the west, the native Reachfolk clans (witchmen and hagraven-led covens among them) resist outsiders from the crags of the Reach; in the east, Eastmarch and ancient Windhelm, the old City of Kings, look toward the Morrowind border. Old Nordic barrows dot the hills.
landmass_lore.cyrodiil: The western Gold Coast of Cyrodiil is a warm, prosperous Colovian land of sea cliffs, vineyards, rolling hills and busy ports. The great harbour city of Anvil looks out over the Abecean Sea, Stirk Isle lies offshore, and Colovian towns, farms and estates follow the coast and hills inland. This is the heart of the Empire: Imperial law, the Nine Divines and Colovian nobility rule here, and pirates and smugglers haunt the Abecean.
landmass_lore.oblivion: This is a plane of Oblivion, shaped by the will of a Daedric Prince rather than by nature. Mortal provinces, Great Houses, Imperial law and ordinary weather mean little here; the realm's master, its Daedra and its own strange rules are what matter.
